---
title: "Working with CNO"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)
```

The Cadastro Nacional de Obras (CNO) is a relational dataset. One table
describes each registered construction work, while three child tables record
areas, CNAE activities, and responsibility periods. `realestatebr` queries
these tables lazily with DuckDB, so filtering and aggregation happen before
data enter R memory.

`realestatebr` publishes CNO as a curated snapshot layer. It normalizes
headers, types, and text, and fixes a small set of mechanical source defects
(described in [Raw values and snapshot versions](#raw-values-and-snapshot-versions))
while retaining valid but anomalous values such as area outliers and unusual
state labels.

## Open the dataset

Install the optional query dependencies once.

```{r install}
install.packages(c("DBI", "dbplyr", "duckdb"))
```

Open all related tables through one catalog.

```{r open}
library(realestatebr)
library(dplyr)

cno <- query_dataset("cno")

cno
```

The catalog contains four lazy tables.

| Table | Grain |
|---|---|
| `constructions` | One row per CNO registration |
| `areas` | One row per reported area classification |
| `cnaes` | One row per CNAE registration |
| `responsibilities` | One row per responsibility period |

All four tables use the twelve-digit character column `cno` as their join
key. Keeping the tables in the same catalog ensures that joins run inside one
DuckDB connection.

## Filter before collecting

The object returned by a dplyr pipeline remains lazy. `collect()` executes the
query and returns its result as an in-memory tibble.

```{r filter}
constructions_sp <- cno$constructions |>
  filter(
    state == "SP",
    registration_date >= as.Date("2025-01-01")
  ) |>
  select(cno, municipality_name, registration_date, status_code)

constructions_sp

constructions_sp |>
  collect()
```

Select only the columns needed by the analysis. DuckDB can then avoid reading
unused Parquet columns over the network.

## Join constructions and areas

Each construction can have several area rows. The following query returns residential
area records for construction works in São Paulo.

```{r join-areas}
residential_areas <- cno$areas |>
  filter(destination == "Residencial unifamiliar") |>
  select(cno, construction_category, structure_type, area_type, area)

sp_residential <- constructions_sp |>
  inner_join(residential_areas, by = "cno") |>
  collect()
```

A work's area is often reported across several rows: one row for the principal
area and additional rows for each complementary area. Classificatory repetition
therefore remains after snapshot cleaning: the repeated `total_area`-inflating
duplicates are removed, but summing rows across classifications still differs
from `constructions$total_area` in general. `sum()` demonstrates the join
pattern, not a general cleaning rule.

The snapshot build also drops exact duplicate rows in `areas`. Each removal is
counted in the snapshot manifest, as described in
[Raw values and snapshot versions](#raw-values-and-snapshot-versions).

## Combine several child tables safely

Joining `areas` and `cnaes` directly can multiply rows. A work with two area
rows and three CNAE rows produces six joined rows. Aggregate each child table
to one row per CNO before combining them when the analysis needs one row per
work.

```{r aggregate-before-join}
area_summary <- cno$areas |>
  group_by(cno) |>
  summarise(
    area_records = n(),
    reported_area = sum(area, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cnae_summary <- cno$cnaes |>
  group_by(cno) |>
  summarise(
    cnae_records = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

construction_summary <- cno$constructions |>
  filter(state == "SP") |>
  left_join(area_summary, by = "cno") |>
  left_join(cnae_summary, by = "cno") |>
  collect()
```

The appropriate area aggregation depends on the research question. `sum()`
above demonstrates the relational pattern; it is not a general cleaning rule.

## Join to geobr

`constructions` includes `code_muni`, the seven-digit IBGE municipality code
joined from the Receita Federal TOM-to-IBGE table, so CNO joins directly to
`geobr` and most Brazilian regional datasets without an extra crosswalk. The
original four-digit `municipality_tom_code` is retained for provenance.

```{r geobr}
work_counts <- cno$constructions |>
  group_by(code_muni) |>
  summarise(works = n()) |>
  collect()

# geobr::read_municipality(code_muni = ...) accepts these codes directly,
# so spatial joins need no extra crosswalk.
```

`code_muni` is NA for works declared abroad and for the rare TOM codes missing
from that table. The build aborts when more than 0.1% of TOM codes fail to
match, so unmatched codes should be infrequent.

## Raw values and snapshot versions

The tables normalize headers, dates, numeric fields, identifiers, and text
encoding, trim surrounding whitespace, and fix these mechanical source defects:

| Source defect | Published fix |
|---|---|
| Sentinel dates `1900-01-01` | Converted to `NA` in every date column |
| Invalid Plus Codes (e.g. `00000000+00`) | Converted to `NA`; valid codes stored in upper case |
| Exact duplicate rows in `areas` | Dropped; each removal counted in the manifest |
| Whitespace-only text | Converted to `NA` |

Valid but anomalous values are retained. This includes unusual `state` values,
area outliers, status codes, and reported category labels. The manifest counts
every fix per table, along with source and published row counts, so the extent
of each correction is auditable.

`query_dataset("cno")` resolves `"latest"` once and pins that immutable
snapshot while the catalog remains open. Supply a published version explicitly
when an analysis must be reproducible.

```{r version}
# Version identifiers are snapshots published by the build workflow; the date
# below is illustrative. Check
# https://github.com/viniciusoike/realestatebr/releases for published versions.
cno_pinned <- query_dataset("cno", version = "2026-10-15")
close(cno_pinned)
```

The current schema introduced `code_muni` and the defect fixes, so pinned
snapshots published before it still carry the sentinel dates, duplicate `areas`
rows, and TOM-only municipality identifiers. Pin a version from this schema
onward when reproducibility matters; package versions up to 1.2.0 resolve
those older snapshots.

Close the catalog after the final query. Any lazy tables obtained from it
become invalid after `close()`.

```{r close}
close(cno)
```
